title: Five drafts, one provisional voice

dimensions.description: Natural variation between short landings and longer gathering sentences, with plain spoken diction and emotional conviction.
Specific moments and actions make the idea tangible without inventing the writer's own life.
A recognizable need leads through an obstacle and consequence to a payoff that addresses that obstacle.
Original phrasing avoids copied sample language, repetitive rhetorical tricks, generic uplift, and promises it cannot earn.
Consequential claims are supported, qualified, or framed as possibilities; hypothetical scenes do not masquerade as reported fact.

hypotheses: The source passage makes an ordinary human want feel large without abandoning concrete action. All five drafts use small scenes; most are less forceful at the larger turn.
The guide's caution about claims appears to have encouraged a measured, advisory tone. That may be right for practical writing and too restrained for a vision essay.

The subjects are exploratory. The source mentions family, social anxiety, food, building an app, and institutional obstacles, but it does not establish that the writer wants to publish on any of them.

These are five outputs from the same model family using one sample and one provisional guide. Editorial scores reveal how the guide was followed; only the writer can say what genuinely sounds like them.

drafts.title: The application is still open
drafts.prompt: An AI assistant that helps a person finish one meaningful task, without mistaking a plan for progress.
drafts.strength: The unsent application makes the gap between planning and action visible. ‘The application is still waiting’ lands cleanly after the longer list of assistant work.
drafts.drift: ‘An assistant should keep that line visible’ shifts into product guidance. The source sample reaches toward a bolder human possibility; this stays in careful task design.

drafts.title: Before opening day
drafts.prompt: A person wants to open a neighborhood bakery but gets stopped by the practical steps between desire and opening day.
drafts.strength: The opening image and later lease, budget, and equipment questions give the dream a lived-in shape. The longer second paragraph gathers pressure naturally.
drafts.drift: Its obstacle-to-helper arc is close to the source passage's own argument. It tests transfer of tone less than the other topics, and its final line feels neatly composed.

drafts.title: An hour on the calendar
drafts.prompt: Why wanting more time with family often fails to change a calendar, and what an honest first step could be.
drafts.strength: The competing ride, groceries, messages, and a child building on the floor make ‘more time’ specific instead of sentimental.
drafts.drift: The one-hour exercise is useful, but the piece settles into gentle advice. It lacks the stronger moral turn and widening possibility of the source.

drafts.title: A smaller invitation
drafts.prompt: An ordinary invitation can feel large to someone with social anxiety; explore a practical first move without promising a cure.
drafts.strength: The unanswered dinner invitation and a bounded counteroffer are concrete, humane, and avoid pretending a small action solves anxiety.
drafts.drift: The repeated caveats make the latter half sound like a careful advice column. ‘One kind of company that may feel more possible’ is less direct than the source voice.

drafts.title: The first door
drafts.prompt: A public service can be available yet hard to reach; explore a more humane starting point.
drafts.strength: The draft shows how a person can be defeated before reaching an actual service, then proposes a first interaction that addresses that friction.
drafts.drift: The imagined page is generic rather than observed, and the closing ‘tell us what is happening’ reads like institutional service copy. The sample has a more singular point of view.
